=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: Two comment-fetch sites in the RB_JUDGE isolation management block — the escalated-handler comment search at approx line 20987 and the latch-clearing comment-recovery search at approx line 21001 (location from the original PR diff; both are in last_run_changed_files) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both `gh api --paginate --slurp` calls to `/issues/*/comments?per_page=100` omit an explicit `sort=created&direction=asc`. GitHub REST API issue-comments endpoint defaults to direction=desc (newest first). With `--slurp`, the resulting paginated array of arrays flattens newest-to-oldest under `.[][]`, so the jq `last` selector that follows picks the oldest matching comment, not the newest.
  WHY: In the escalated-handler path, if multiple isolation markers match the same head (due to comment-response recovery creating a duplicate post), `last` selects the oldest matching ID instead of the newest, and the comment_id stored in state points to stale evidence. In the latch-clearing recovery path, if a lost POST left one marker from a prior run and a subsequent run posted another, the verification step examines the older comment and its `created_at` instead of the newest, and the ownership check can fail even though a valid newer marker exists — leaving `ai:needs-human` set indefinitely on a new-head PR that should resume. The fix is adding `sort=created&direction=asc` to both `gh api` URLs, matching the existing pattern at line 13602.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Lost-comment recovery jq filters (~line 20987-21007 and 21020-21026 in the new code) that use `[.[][] | select(...)] | last` on paginated `gh api --paginate --slurp` output for issue comments and events
  PROBLEM: The new RB_JUDGE isolation recovery code relies on `| last` to select the newest comment/event without explicit jq `sort_by(.created_at)`.
  WHY: GitHub's API returns issue comments and events in ascending chronological order by default, so `last` = newest in practice, but the inconsistency is fragile if API behavior or pagination ordering ever changes. Suggested minimal fix: Add `| sort_by(.created_at // "")` before `| last` in the three jq filters that use `[.[][] | select(...)] | last` in the isolation latch recovery path, matching the pattern used at line 15867. The review states this is a consistency concern, not a runtime bug.
